name: Wangkumara
catalog_quote: Primary stress occurs normally on the first syllable of a word, with secondary stress on third and fifth syllables - except that final syllables are unstressed in connected speech. ... Many stems heard in citation form have pronounced stress on the final syllable as well as strong final aspiration (described by the informant as final 'h'). These features are absent in connected speech, except at …

audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding passage (M&W 1979:5 section 2.1) is verbatim in the held PL-B65 text/PDF at the stated page, but it sits only in dq/dloc; quote/cite/loc/grade are blank, so the record should be upgraded by copying the verified primary quotation into the formal fields with cite 'McDonald & Wurm 1979' and loc 'p.5 section 2.1 (PDF p.15)'. Coding check: the source states fixed initial primary stress with rhythmic secondary stress on 3rd/5th syllables, final syllables unstressed in connected speech, final stress+aspiration in citation forms analysed by the authors themselves as utterance-final/emphatic suprasegmentals, and a morphological override (first syllable of a disyllabic suffix takes secondary stress). 'fixed-dominant' (dom=true, strict=false) and domain LUMPED are exactly what this passage supports; the existing corr notes already record the citation-vs-connected-speech sp
